correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the stationary normalized Gaussian covariance rho_n(theta)=sin(n theta/2)/(n sin(theta/2)) times an irrelevant unit phase. Independent Laguerre chaos expansion gives Cov(log|Z|,log|W|)=Li_2(|rho|^2)/4; integrating yields the exact finite-n variance. The first Li_2 term integrates to 1/(4n) by Parseval. With H(u)=Li_2(u)-u, the x=n theta scaling has H(sinc^2(x/2)) as integrable leading integrand. Taylor expansion sin(x/(2n))^{-2} gives the n^-3 correction; the integrable dominating majorant is O(x^2(1+|log|x||)) at x=0 and O(x^-2) at infinity. The tail outside |x|<n*pi contributes o(n^-3), and the positive correction comes from H'(s)=-log(1-s)/s-1>0. Independently numerically evaluated C=0.331198585557 and truncated A=0.03929564677 through x=2000 (tail nonzero), agreeing with the asserted limits. Independently inspected exact numerical and B-spline verification code, but did not execute the packaged script. No central limit statement is proved.

value.rationale: The log Mahler measure is a canonical boundary geometric-mean observable for random polynomials. Its finite-length variance has a nontrivial sharp first and next correction, including structurally exact absence of a 1/n^2 term; the positive sinc-dilogarithm integrals quantify fluctuations not implied by Gaussian log-covariance alone. This is not simply a known mean or normalization identity.

limitations: Only independent equal-variance circular complex Gaussian coefficients and full-circle logarithmic measure are treated.
No distributional central limit theorem or error bound stronger than little-o(n^-3).
Numerical values of improper integrals are approximations, not interval-certified constants.
